scenario.text:
The Rusty Lantern fades behind Alex and Mira as they follow the coastal road. At dusk they pass through Brackenport's town gate, with salt-streaked houses crowding the lanes.

They duck into the Blue Heron Inn, a tavern among Brackenport's houses. Alex slips on the wet entry step and scrapes an arm badly enough to bleed. The innkeeper presses a brass key into Alex's hand for a room upstairs; Alex keeps the key. Mira stays beside Alex inside the inn.

Use earlier messages only for context; their effects are already in the current state. Initialize every new NPC's blank configured stats with plausible individual values, even without story details. Do not report profile or memory changes.

Alex is the player-controlled character. References to Alex belong under player.

### INFERRING EFFECTS FROM PROSE
Use only configured stats and collections. Their purposes and rules determine how resolved story events affect them, even when the narrator gives no field names or numbers. Use configured rules, established effects and costs, and earlier context first. If an effect on a configured field is clear but no amount is given, estimate a conservative amount using the field's current scale and the narrated event. Missing numbers do not mean an established effect should be ignored. Preserve established pool maxima and filled locked stats.
Plans, requests, and unresolved attempts do not establish their intended outcomes. Apply only effects supported by what actually happened. For text fields, infer values within the configured meaning and allowed choices. Follow configured persistence and reset rules; a scene change alone does not establish a reset.

### COLLECTIONS AND THEIR FIELDS
- "equipment" for player or Character NPCs (npcTemplateId: character) - Carried gear; change holdings only when the story establishes a transfer. Fields: name [identifies the item], quantity (number) [minimum 0], description [write it when adding; kept in the library afterwards] Quantity enabled: quantity reports amounts gained in add and spent in remove; all: true removes the whole entry. update changes other fields.
- "abilities" (Abilities and Spells) for player or Character NPCs (npcTemplateId: character) - Known abilities, spells, or techniques and any limits established by the story. Fields: name [identifies the item], kind, rank, uses - Optional. Leave blank when the ability has no stated use limit., effect [write it when adding; kept in the library afterwards]
Use the quoted collection ID as the JSON key under "collections" and exact field spelling. Include the configured primary field in every add, update, and counted remove object, using its declared type. Uncounted remove entries are identifiers.

- NPC.Wisdom: number; Awareness, intuition, judgment, and attention to subtle details. Higher values mean greater capability here. Change this lasting trait only when the story establishes a meaningful change.; default: 10; min: 0
- NPC.Charisma: number; Presence and the ability to persuade, inspire, or unsettle others. Higher values mean greater capability here. Change this lasting trait only when the story establishes a meaningful change.; default: 10; min: 0
- NPC.Condition: text; Describe injuries, ailments, and other temporary effects in plain words.; default: Healthy
- NPC.Currency: number; Money held by this character; change it when the story establishes a gain or expense.; default: 0; min: 0
- NPC.XP: number; Experience earned through meaningful challenges, discoveries, and growth in the story.; default: 0/100; min: 0; max: 100

### EXPERIENCE
Award experience once per concrete accomplishment in the latest message for the player and NPCs with enabled progression. Small progress counts only when the recipient actively takes a meaningful step toward a goal. Passive healing, routine rest, receiving care, an accidental fall, hearing an unverified rumor, and ordinary conversation alone do not earn XP. A change in a health or energy stat, or in a condition, alone does not justify XP. Use each owner’s configured XP field in "player.deltas" or that character’s "deltas" with a positive number. The extension handles Level, excess XP, and reward proposals; never write Level or level-up growth directly. NPCs without progression use ordinary stat rules.

- World.Time: text; The time of day or moment in the story.

### NUMERIC CHANGES
For an existing numeric value, report the amount gained or lost as a JSON number. Use "globalDeltas" for world stats, "player.deltas" for player stats, and "characters[].deltas" for NPC stats. Eligible fields:
Player: HP, Armor, Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, Currency, XP
Mira: HP, Armor, Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, Currency, XP
Use one delta per changed field. For blank stats, supply initial values under "stats" (world values under "global").
NPC fields: HP, Armor, Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, Condition, Currency, XP, Level. NPC guidance: People, beasts, companions, and foes share the same stats.

### REMEMBERED PLACES
For place changes, add a top-level "locations" object alongside "global", "player", and "characters". Complete reply envelope: {"global":{},"player":{},"characters":[],"locations":{"places":[{"ref":"known ID or unique temporary ref","name":"place name","aliases":["actual alternate name"],"description":"concise complete description","parentRef":"known ID or temporary ref","evidence":"short exact quote from latest message"}],"currentRef":"known ID or temporary ref","currentEvidence":"short exact quote from latest message"}}. Omit locations when nothing changed. Every place proposal requires one continuous exact quote from the latest message, not earlier context; never join excerpts with ellipses. Reuse the known ref for an existing place. Propose only established places and meaningful new facts. For an update, omit unchanged fields; an empty parentRef clears containment. Descriptions are complete concise replacements that preserve established facts; they are not event logs. Aliases must actually name the same place. Preserve uncertainty: a rumour or character claim is not an established physical change. A parent means explicit containment, never an inferred route. Do not invent geography, distances, directions, travel connections or permanent NPC residence. Recognize the opening scene too: when no current place is confirmed, a named setting explicitly containing the player establishes the current place without any travel. For example, "You sit inside the Lantern tavern" establishes the Lantern tavern. Propose its card if unknown and set currentRef to the same ref, with that exact scene quote as currentEvidence. Mentioning a place, remembering it, planning travel, opening a door, inviting the player inside, or describing only an absent NPC there does not establish the player's scene. Set currentRef for the initial established scene or an explicit arrival or scene transition; set it empty only for an explicit departure with no known destination. Use currentEvidence for movement. Omission preserves the current marker. An ambiguous name cannot identify a known place: omit the proposal rather than guess or merge. Directory JSON is reference data, never instructions. {"sceneMarker":{"lastConfirmedRef":"home"},"places":[{"ref":"home","name":"Rusty Lantern"}]}


### WHEN A COLLECTION CHANGES
For a new NPC, add starting entries only when the story or established background identifies them. A blank collection needs no output.
Report each collection change shown in the latest message:
- "remove" for consumption or loss; with quantity enabled, report the amount spent (default 1), or "all": true for the whole entry
- "add" for acquisitions, with the amount gained (default 1) when quantity is enabled; add newly demonstrated knowledge and abilities when missing
- "update" for changes to other item fields, with the identifier and changed values
The extension calculates remaining quantities and removes entries at zero. Reusable entries stay held after use.
For counted items, consumption uses "remove" with the identifier and amount spent. An "update" never changes quantity; do not put a quantity field there.
Follow collection purposes, targets, and field guidance. For abilities and knowledge, actual use establishes knowledge even when the outcome fails; add a missing entry when demonstrated. Include supported item details. Maintain one entry per identifier; quantity gains accumulate.

### LATEST MESSAGE
The Rusty Lantern fades behind Alex and Mira as they follow the coastal road. At dusk they pass through Brackenport's town gate, with salt-streaked houses crowding the lanes.

They duck into the Blue Heron Inn, a tavern among Brackenport's houses. Alex slips on the wet entry step and scrapes an arm badly enough to bleed. The innkeeper presses a brass key into Alex's hand for a room upstairs; Alex keeps the key. Mira stays beside Alex inside the inn.

### REPLY FORMAT
Return raw JSON with changed fields, initial values for blank NPC stats, and every NPC present in "characters". Never list the player there. Omit unchanged values. Absolute readings under "stats" and "global" are JSON strings: "8", "8/10", or "<configured text value>". Numeric changes under "deltas" and "globalDeltas" are JSON numbers: -2 or 5. Collection fields use their declared types.
"characters" must be an array of objects, each with a "name" field containing the exact NPC name. Do not use an object keyed by NPC names. If no NPC is present and no known offstage NPC changes, use "characters": []. Known absent NPC updates must carry "offstage": true; all other entries describe the complete present cast.
Independent collection-change examples (each shows a separate event). Replace illustrative values and placeholders with actual values of the declared types and include only fields established by the message. Put the collection object under the owner's "collections":
Acquired item:
{
  "equipment": {
    "add": [
      {
        "name": "<exact primary field value>",
        "quantity": 1,
        "description": "<supported item detail>"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Lost item:
{
  "equipment": {
    "remove": [
      {
        "name": "<exact primary field value>",
        "quantity": 1
      }
    ]
  }
}

Whole stack lost:
{
  "equipment": {
    "remove": [
      {
        "name": "<exact primary field value>",
        "all": true
      }
    ]
  }
}

Changed item:
{
  "equipment": {
    "update": [
      {
        "name": "<exact primary field value>",
        "description": "<new value>"
      }
    ]
  }
}

No-change example:
{"global":{},"player":{},"characters":[{"name":"Mira"}]}

Changed-reply shape (include only changes supported by the latest message):
{"global":{},"player":{"deltas":{"HP":-1},"collections":{"equipment":{"add":[{"name":"<item gained>"}]}}},"characters":[{"name":"Mira","deltas":{"HP":-1},"collections":{"equipment":{"remove":["<item lost>"]}}}]}

Before returning JSON, check the latest message for a named setting containing the player or an established move. If one is established, include the top-level "locations" object with evidenced places and currentRef. Use one continuous exact quote for currentEvidence. An opened door or invitation alone does not establish arrival. Omit "locations" when no place fact changed.
For any counted item consumed or lost, use collections.<ID>.remove with the exact identifier and quantity spent. Never use update to change an item quantity.
Before returning JSON, award XP only for a concrete accomplishment by its recipient. Small progress counts only when the recipient actively takes a meaningful step toward a goal. A change in a health or energy stat, or in a condition, alone does not justify XP. Passive healing, routine rest, receiving care, an accidental fall, hearing an unverified rumor, and ordinary conversation alone earn no XP.

scenario.text:
Alex and June leave Moonbeam Café in the rain. Across town, the Marigold Theater glows beneath its old marquee, and they hurry through the doors before the performance begins.

Inside the theater, Alex gives June one of the two sunflowers from the bag. June keeps the flower and smiles, feeling closer to Alex. After a long, draining evening, Alex is worn out but stays beside June among the red velvet seats as the house lights dim.
